newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU set to grant Belgrade trade privileges.
newsitem.headline: EU set to grant Belgrade trade privileges.

text.p: European Union foreign ministers are likely to grant trade privileges to the rump-Yugoslavia next week to try to coax it into more democratic reforms, diplomats said.
The issue would be discussed when the ministers met in Luxembourg next Tuesday, they said.
The ministers will tie implementation of trade preferences allowing some Yugoslav industrial goods duty-free access to EU markets to respect of human rights and tolerance of opposition groups.
The privileges would also relax restrictions on the quantity of Yugoslav goods entering the EU.
EU officials fear a failure to grant trade concessions to Yugoslavia -- now made up of Serbia and Montenegro -- could contribute to a total economic collapse of the country.
The Yugoslav economy has been shattered by a four-year trade embargo.
The government of President Slobodan Milosevic is struggling to dismantle an "outer wall" of remaining sanctions and gain access to urgently needed capital to revive its stagnant economy.

The United Nations slapped a trade embargo on Belgrade in 1992 for its role in the Bosnian war. It was lifted last October, but the outer wall was left in place while Serbia's behaviour was monitored, particularly in mostly-Albanian province of Kosovo.
